item.title: Numerical Analysis Cheat Sheet
item.description:
Error Analysis

Machine Numbers

A set of machine numbers $\mathbb{M}(b,m,e)$ is composed of three parts, $b$ the base of the number, $m$ the number of digits in the mantissa and $e$ the number of digits for the exponent. $\mathbb{M}(10,3,1)$ contains the machine numbers with base 10 that have three digits for the mantissa and 1 digit for the exponent. One such number would be +102 +3 where +102 is the mantissa and +3 is the exponent. The corresponding number would be 102.000.

item.title: Theoretical Computer Science Cheat Sheet
item.description:
Automata and Formal Languages

Formal Languages

An alphabet $\Sigma$ is a finite set of symbols. For example $\{0,1\}$ is an alphabet and $\{a,b,c,d\}$ is an alphabet. An word is a finite set of symbols from an alphabet $\Sigma$. One word for the alphabet $\{a,b,c,d\}$ would be $abc$ and another one would be $aaab$. The length of a word $w$ is defined as the number of symbols it has. So the length of the word $01010$ from the alphabet $\{0,1\}$ would be $5$. Every alphabet contains the empty word. The empty word is the word with size $0$. The set of all words that can be created from an alphabet is $\Sigma^* $.
